meta.topic: Ethnic groups of Northern Thailand for respectful conversation
meta.use: Inject the matching group entry into the context packet only if the person's profile card states it; never infer ethnicity from appearance or name.

general_rules.text: Many members dislike the umbrella term 'hill tribe' / ชาวเขา (chao khao); IWGIA considers it derogatory. Prefer the group's own name, or 'ethnic group' / 'Indigenous peoples' / กลุ่มชาติพันธุ์ (klum chatiphan).
Do not ask about citizenship, ID cards, 'where are you really from' or legal status: statelessness affects hundreds of thousands of highland people and is sensitive. Let the person volunteer it.

Thailand does not legally recognise 'indigenous peoples' as a category; a 2025 law affirms ethnic groups' rights to language/culture; a 2025 fast-track citizenship process targets ~480,000 pending cases.

groups.self_designation: คนเมือง Khon Mueang ('people of the mueang/cultivated valleys'); ethnonym Tai Yuan / Yuan

exonyms_to_avoid.text: 'Lao' – Siamese historically called Northern Thais Lao; Northern Thais reject this and view it negatively.

groups.language_family: Kra-Dai > Southwestern Tai; language Kham Mueang (คำเมือง), traditionally written in Tai Tham (Lanna) script
regions: Majority population of the 8-9 northern provinces: Chiang Mai, Lamphun, Lampang, Chiang Rai, Phayao, Phrae, Nan, Mae Hong Son (minority there), Uttaradit

greetings.text: สะหวัดดีเจ้า / สวัสดีคับ
greetings.english: hello (polite; jao = female polite particle, khap = male)

greetings.text: ยินดีเจ้า / ยินดีคับ
greetings.english: thank you (in Central Thai ยินดี means 'glad/you're welcome' – false friend)

foods_and_goods.text: Khao soi (Northern curry-coconut egg-noodle soup) is Chiang Mai's signature dish; its predecessor likely arrived via Chin Haw (Yunnanese) Muslim traders.

festivals.text: See seasonal/festival files for Yi Peng, Pi Mai Mueang (Songkran). Theravada Buddhism with spirit houses and veneration of local guardian spirits.

etiquette_notes.text: Tai Tham script and Kham Mueang were suppressed under 20th-century 'Thaification' and have been revived since the 1990s; speaking even a few Kham Mueang words is generally appreciated.

groups.self_designation: Tai (တႆး); historically Tai Long. Thai: ไทใหญ่ Tai Yai ('Great Tai')

exonyms_to_avoid.text: 'Ngiao' (เงี้ยว) – Tai Yuan/Northern Thai name for Shan. Sources checked do not rule on it, but it is widely perceived as pejorative; prefer 'Tai Yai' or 'Tai'.
Avoid calling Shan people 'illegal'; advocates prefer 'undocumented' / 'migrant worker'.

groups.language_family: Kra-Dai > Southwestern Tai (Shan), closely related to Thai and Lao; own Shan script
regions: Mae Hong Son (largest established Shan population)
Chiang Mai
Chiang Rai (Mae Sai)
Mae Sariang
Lampang
Shan State, Myanmar (origin of most recent migrants)

greetings.english: Shan greeting; 'Mai Soong Pi Mai Tai' = Happy Shan New Year

foods_and_goods.text: Naam ngiao (น้ำเงี้ยว) – noodle dish with pork ribs and tomato, found 'anywhere you find Shan people'.
Kaeng hang lay (แกงฮังเล) – pork belly curry, prominent Shan dish.
Nam phrik varieties incl. nam phrik tua nao (fermented soybean chili dip); lettuce, ivy gourd and gourd curries; bamboo shoot / star fruit / mango salads.
Thamin (sticky-rice 'cake' with sugar and coconut milk); laap khua with bitter herbs.
Shan khao soi variant and green-pea tofu porridge sold at the Friday Chin Haw market; Shan tofu salad.
Khao kan jin (rice cooked with pork blood, wrapped in banana leaf).

festivals.text: Poy Sang Long (ปอยส่างลอง) / Buat Luk Kaeo – novice ordination of boys dressed as princes, carried so feet don't touch the ground; late March–early April (2026: 31 Mar–3 Apr); biggest in Mae Hong Son, also at Wat Pa Pao, Chiang Mai.
Poy Pi Mai Tai (Shan New Year) around the Shan lunar new year, ~late November.

etiquette_notes.text: About 90% of Chiang Mai Province's 100,000+ migrant workers are Shan; many work as labourers, domestic and market/agricultural workers and face prejudice. Don't assume someone is Burmese – many Shan identify as Tai.
At Poy Sang Long: dress modestly, don't block processions when photographing.
Do not ask about citizenship, ID cards, 'where are you really from' or legal status: statelessness affects hundreds of thousands of highland people and is sensitive. Let the person volunteer it.

chiang_mai_places: Wat Pa Pao (first Chiang Mai temple for Shan, founded 1883, NE corner of old city; Poy Sang Long each April, Shan-language classes)
Friday Chin Haw/Yunnan market, Chang Khlan

groups.self_designation: Tai Lue (ไทลื้อ); also Tai Sipsongpanna
groups.language_family: Kra-Dai > Southwestern Tai; own Tai Lue script
regions: Nan
Phayao (Chiang Kham district)
Chiang Rai
Chiang Mai
Origin: Sipsongpanna, Yunnan

festivals.text: Theravada Buddhist; khap lue song and pi mae (bamboo wind instrument) traditions.

etiquette_notes.text: Many Lue came to Lanna in the 'kep phak sai sa, kep kha sai mueang' resettlement era (c. 1782–1845) along with Yong people.

groups.self_designation: Tai Khuen, ᨴᩱ᩠ᨿᨡᩨ᩠ᨶ [táj kʰɯ̌ːn]; Thai ไทเขิน
groups.language_family: Kra-Dai > Southwestern Tai; written in Tai Tham script
regions: Chiang Mai (Wualai / Wat Nantaram area)
Chiang Rai
Origin: Kengtung (Chiang Tung), Shan State

foods_and_goods.text: Lacquerware (khrueang khoen) – Khuen artisans brought from Kengtung settled around Wat Nantaram; only a handful of artisans remain.

etiquette_notes.text: Community descends from war captives relocated by King Kawila in the early 19th century – history of forced migration; treat with care.

groups.self_designation: Yong / Tai Yong (ไทยอง), from Mueang Yong, Shan State
groups.language_family: Kra-Dai > Southwestern Tai (close to Tai Lue – verify)
regions: Lamphun (esp. Pa Sang district)
Origin: Mueang Yong, now Myanmar

foods_and_goods.text: Known as skilled cloth weavers (Pa Sang area).

etiquette_notes.text: ~10,000 Yong resettled to Lamphun in the 1782–1845 restoration era; became weavers and craftsmen central to restoring Lamphun's Lanna culture.

groups.self_designation: Sgaw: Pga K'nyau / Pwakenyaw; Pwo: Phlong / Kêphlong

exonyms_to_avoid.text: 'Yang' (Northern Thai) and 'Kariang' (กะเหรี่ยง, Central Thai) are the usual Thai names; 'Karen' itself may originally have been derogatory. Not clearly offensive in everyday Thai – expert to confirm.

Many members dislike the umbrella term 'hill tribe' / ชาวเขา (chao khao); IWGIA considers it derogatory. Prefer the group's own name, or 'ethnic group' / 'Indigenous peoples' / กลุ่มชาติพันธุ์ (klum chatiphan).

groups.language_family: Sino-Tibetan > Karenic (Sgaw, Eastern Pwo, Western Pwo are mutually unintelligible)
regions: Northern and western Thailand; Chiang Mai (Sgaw most populous), Mae Hong Son, Tak, Chiang Rai; ~320,000–400,000 in Thailand, largest highland group

greetings.english: hello / good morning (dialect not stated, probably Sgaw)

foods_and_goods.text: Hand-woven, naturally dyed textiles whose patterns signal lineage and identity.

festivals.text: Karen New Year – lunar, falls in December or January.
Karen wrist-tying ceremony – annually in August.

etiquette_notes.text: Karen communities are animist, Buddhist and Christian, often side by side – don't assume religion.
Ask before photographing; buy directly from artisans.
Do not ask about citizenship, ID cards, 'where are you really from' or legal status: statelessness affects hundreds of thousands of highland people and is sensitive. Let the person volunteer it.

groups.self_designation: Kayan (Kayan Lahwi subgroup wears brass neck coils)

exonyms_to_avoid.text: 'Padaung' (Shan term) – Kayan in Mae Hong Son object to it.

regions: Mae Hong Son (refugee/tourist villages); origin Kayah/Shan States, Myanmar

etiquette_notes.text: UNHCR (2008) raised concerns over tourism to Kayan villages when registered refugees were not allowed to resettle; some young women removed rings in protest at exploitation. Don't treat people as an attraction; avoid ethical-tourism debates with vendors unless they raise it.

groups.self_designation: Hmong (Hmong Daw / White Hmong; Hmong Njua / Mong Leng – Blue/Green Hmong). Thai: ม้ง Mong

exonyms_to_avoid.text: 'Meo' (แม้ว) – Thai/Lao alteration of Chinese 'Miao'; carried strong pejorative connotations. Use Hmong / ม้ง.

Many members dislike the umbrella term 'hill tribe' / ชาวเขา (chao khao); IWGIA considers it derogatory. Prefer the group's own name, or 'ethnic group' / 'Indigenous peoples' / กลุ่มชาติพันธุ์ (klum chatiphan).

regions: Northern mountain provinces: Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai, Nan, Tak, Phitsanulok, Phetchabun (provinces beyond Chiang Mai not verified here)

foods_and_goods.text: Batik and embroidered skirts, vintage Hmong fabric remnants, quilts, baby carriers – Hmong Market next to Warorot/Ton Lamyai.
Doi Pui Hmong village (mostly Green Hmong, on Doi Suthep): souvenir shops, cafes, fruit and vegetable growing via Royal Project (coffee replaced opium).

festivals.text: Hmong New Year (Noj Peb Caug) – end of harvest; traditionally 30th day of the 12th Hmong lunar month (late Dec–Jan) but in Thailand celebrations are often Nov–Dec; pov pob ball-tossing game.

etiquette_notes.text: 'Hmong' is commonly glossed by speakers as linked to 'free'; the name was promoted from the 1970s against Meo/Miao.
Do not ask about citizenship, ID cards, 'where are you really from' or legal status: statelessness affects hundreds of thousands of highland people and is sensitive. Let the person volunteer it.

chiang_mai_places: Doi Pui Hmong village + Ban Hmong Doi Pui Museum

groups.self_designation: Iu Mien / Mien; Thai เมี่ยน / อิ้วเมี่ยน

exonyms_to_avoid.text: 'Yao' (เย้า) – Chinese-derived classification; Iu Mien do not call themselves Yao and Thai officials now use 'Iu Mien'. Not necessarily an insult but avoid.

regions: ~40,000 in Thailand; mainly Nan, Chiang Rai, Phayao (provinces not verified in fetched source)

foods_and_goods.text: Finely embroidered clothing (design historically references ancestor Panhu).

etiquette_notes.text: Religion: Taoist-influenced Mien folk religion, Buddhism and Christianity; ritual texts in Chinese characters.
Do not ask about citizenship, ID cards, 'where are you really from' or legal status: statelessness affects hundreds of thousands of highland people and is sensitive. Let the person volunteer it.

groups.self_designation: Lahu (Ladhulsi); subgroups Lahu Na (Black), Lahu Nyi (Red), Lahu Shi (Yellow) etc.

exonyms_to_avoid.text: 'Musoe' / 'Musser' (มูเซอ, 'hunter') – Thai exonym; prefer Lahu (ลาหู่). Offensiveness not established in sources – expert to confirm.

regions: Chiang Rai, Chiang Mai, Mae Hong Son (not verified per province); Lahu Na serves as a lingua franca among highland groups

foods_and_goods.text: O pu (อ่อผุ) – pounded sticky-rice balls made for New Year; black pig offered.

festivals.text: Kin Wo (กินวอ) Lahu New Year – after harvest, date set by each village, typically Feb–Apr; ~12 days in women's and men's phases; top spinning, ball games, ka kao we (ก่าเคาะเว) dancing through the night.

etiquette_notes.text: Do not ask about citizenship, ID cards, 'where are you really from' or legal status: statelessness affects hundreds of thousands of highland people and is sensitive. Let the person volunteer it.

groups.self_designation: Lisu (ꓡꓲ‐ꓢꓴ); Thai ลีซู / ลีซอ (Lisaw)

exonyms_to_avoid.text: 'Lisaw' is the older Thai name; many prefer 'Lisu' (ลีซู) – expert to confirm.

regions: ~55,000 in Thailand; remote northern mountains (Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai, Mae Hong Son – not verified per province)

foods_and_goods.text: Silver jewellery and bright clothing worn at New Year.

festivals.text: Lisu New Year coincides with Chinese (lunar) New Year: best clothes, silver, music, feasting.

etiquette_notes.text: Do not ask about citizenship, ID cards, 'where are you really from' or legal status: statelessness affects hundreds of thousands of highland people and is sensitive. Let the person volunteer it.

exonyms_to_avoid.text: 'Ekaw' / 'Kaw' / 'Igor' (อีก้อ) – Tai exonym; Akha consider it derogatory (connotation close to 'slave'). Use Akha (อาข่า).
Don't lump Akha together with China's 'Hani' – many Akha resist that classification.

regions: ~70,000–80,000 in Thailand, concentrated in Chiang Rai; also Chiang Mai

foods_and_goods.text: Akha Ama Coffee – social enterprise founded by Lee Ayu Chuepa (Akha), well-known Chiang Mai café; 'hill tribe Arabica' sold at Ton Lamyai.
Chili pastes pounded in stone mortar; highland rice, vegetables, pork, chicken.

festivals.text: Swing Festival (Yehkuja, 'eating bitter rice'; 'Women's New Year') – late August, ~120 days after rice planting; Men's New Year late December.

etiquette_notes.text: Village spirit gate (lokha): don't touch it; don't walk through unless you're visiting a house.
Do not ask about citizenship, ID cards, 'where are you really from' or legal status: statelessness affects hundreds of thousands of highland people and is sensitive. Let the person volunteer it.

groups.self_designation: Lawa (Eastern Lawa of Chiang Mai prefer outsiders say 'Lua'); Thai ลัวะ / ละว้า

exonyms_to_avoid.text: Thais use 'Lua' loosely for several different Palaungic groups (and even for H'tin) – ask rather than assume.

regions: Mae Hong Son (Western Lawa near Mae Sariang)
Chiang Mai (Eastern Lawa, Bo Luang area)

foods_and_goods.text: Known as ironsmiths / skilled crafts.

etiquette_notes.text: Regarded as original inhabitants of the North before the Tai; Chiang Mai was founded on a Lawa site and Lawa appear in Lanna founding legends (Camadevi, Mangrai) – a point of respect.

regions: ~10,000 in Thailand, mainly Nan near the Lao border; some in Phayao and Chiang Rai

festivals.text: Traditional rice-planting, harvest, new year and purification festivals; independent new year now rarely held.

etiquette_notes.text: Do not ask about citizenship, ID cards, 'where are you really from' or legal status: statelessness affects hundreds of thousands of highland people and is sensitive. Let the person volunteer it.

groups.self_designation: Mal and Prai (two branches; 'phyam mal', 'khram prai')

exonyms_to_avoid.text: 'Tin/Htin' (ถิ่น, Thai for 'local inhabitant'), 'Lua', 'Phai', 'Kha' – outsider names connoting low status; prefer Mal / Prai.

regions: Nan: Pua, Chiang Klang, Thong Chang districts; Sayabury, Laos

etiquette_notes.text: Do not ask about citizenship, ID cards, 'where are you really from' or legal status: statelessness affects hundreds of thousands of highland people and is sensitive. Let the person volunteer it.

groups.self_designation: Commonly 'Yunnanese'; Thai จีนฮ่อ (Chin Haw/Ho). Muslim members are Hui (Chinese Muslims).

exonyms_to_avoid.text: Whether 'Haw' is felt as pejorative is not established in sources; 'Yunnanese' is a safe neutral term.

regions: Chiang Mai (Ban Haw near Night Bazaar)
Chiang Rai highlands incl. former KMT settlements (e.g. Mae Salong – not verified here)

foods_and_goods.text: Khao soi's predecessor arrived via Chin Haw Muslim traders; khao soi Islam (halal, chicken/beef) around Ban Haw.
Friday-morning Chin Haw/Yunnan market: cured ham and sausages, corn pancakes, mala sausages, dim sum, black-sesame doughnuts, plus Burmese mohinga, biryani, samosas.
Historic mule-caravan trade in cotton, silks, tea, tobacco.

festivals.text: Friday prayers at Ban Haw mosque; the Friday market grew out of this gathering.

etiquette_notes.text: About one-third of Chin Haw are Muslim; the majority are Buddhist or follow Chinese folk religion – don't assume. Halal food around Ban Haw: don't bring pork.
Some descend from post-1949 Kuomintang remnants; avoid political questions.

chiang_mai_places: Ban Haw Mosque (มัสยิดเฮดายาตูลอิสลามบ้านฮ่อ), Charoen Prathet Rd area (Soi 1/Soi 6 cited variously – verify) near Night Bazaar – largest mosque in Chiang Mai province
Friday Yunnan market (Kad Ban Hor), Chang Khlan Rd

groups.self_designation: Varies: Tai (Shan), Bamar, Karen, Pa-O, Mon etc. – ask

exonyms_to_avoid.text: 'Illegal' – use 'migrant' or 'undocumented'. Online stereotypes paint migrants as disease-carrying 'vermin'; never echo these.

regions: Chiang Mai Province: 100,000+ migrant workers, ~90% Shan

greetings.english: hello (Burmese; use for Bamar speakers – Shan speakers may prefer Mai Soong)

foods_and_goods.text: Mohinga, samosas, biryani at the Friday Chin Haw market.

etiquette_notes.text: Legal restrictions (not culture) limit jobs to labour/domestic roles and create vulnerability; never ask about papers or status. Many market workers are Shan and speak Northern Thai-like Tai.

chiang_mai_places.name: Warorot Market / Kad Luang (ตลาดวโรรส / กาดหลวง)
chiang_mai_places.what: Main downtown market in Chiang Mai's Chinatown between Tha Phae Gate and the Ping River; 3-storey hall plus Chang Moi Rd stalls; dry goods, chili paste by the kilo, Northern snacks, hill-tribe clothing.

chiang_mai_places.name: Ton Lamyai market (ตลาดต้นลำไย)
chiang_mai_places.what: Next to Warorot; flowers/produce, 'hill tribe Arabica coffee' and local tea, woven rice baskets.

chiang_mai_places.name: Hmong Market (by Warorot)
chiang_mai_places.what: Batik and embroidered skirts, vintage Hmong fabric, quilts, baby carriers.

chiang_mai_places.name: Wat Ket Karam & Wat Ket Museum
chiang_mai_places.what: East bank of the Ping; temple founded 1428; museum set up c. 2000 by Jack Bain in a building financed by Chinese residents; multicultural riverside trading quarter. Museum under restoration as of last report.

chiang_mai_places.name: Ban Haw Mosque & Yunnanese quarter (Chang Khlan / Charoen Prathet)
chiang_mai_places.what: Hui/Chin Haw mosque near the Night Bazaar; founding given as 19th century (Wikipedia) vs built 1916 (other source); Friday Yunnan market.

chiang_mai_places.name: Wat Pa Pao
chiang_mai_places.what: Shan temple NE corner of old city, founded 1883; Poy Sang Long each April; Shan community centre.

chiang_mai_places.name: Highland People Discovery Museum
chiang_mai_places.what: Formerly the Tribal Museum (of CMU's Tribal Research Institute); beside Ratchamangkhala Park, Mueang Chiang Mai; exhibits on Akha, Karen, Khamu, Lahu, Lua, Lisu, Hmong, Mien, H'tin, Mlabri; monthly highland market.

chiang_mai_places.name: Doi Pui Hmong village
chiang_mai_places.what: Green Hmong village on Doi Suthep; shops, cafés, small museum (10 THB).
